vuln.name: API Key / Secret Token Exposure
vuln.description: An API key, secret token, or credential appears in a response body, URL parameter, or client-reachable resource. Keys may be cloud provider keys, third-party API keys, or internal access tokens.
vuln.impact: A leaked key grants the holder whatever permissions the key carries — often read or write access to cloud storage, databases, payment providers, or the application's own APIs. Cloud keys are routinely automated for cryptomining or data exfiltration within minutes.
vuln.recommendation: Remove the key from any client-visible surface. Rotate the exposed key immediately, restrict it by IP or scope, and store secrets server-side in a secrets manager rather than in client code or responses.
